================================================================================

  This file is a STARTING POINT drafted by an engineer, not a lawyer. It has no
  legal review behind it and it is not legal advice.

  Before the first client handover, the owner must:

    1. Have this reviewed or redrafted by a qualified lawyer in the governing
       jurisdiction (Tanzania, or wherever the contracting entity sits).
    2. Fill in every <PLACEHOLDER>.
    3. Delete this banner.

  Why it matters more than it looks: a Docker image is a container for compiled
  files, not a protection mechanism. Anyone holding the image can extract the
  application and decompile it. This document, and the contract it sits under,
  is the actual thing restricting what a client may do with the software.
  See dist/README.md for the honest technical picture.

================================================================================

   Scope of permitted use: <NUMBER OF INSTALLATIONS / SITES / NAMED USERS>.


2. RESTRICTIONS

   The Licensee shall not:

   a) copy, distribute, sublicense, sell, rent, lease or otherwise make the
      Software available to any third party;

   b) decompile, disassemble, reverse engineer or otherwise attempt to derive
      the source code, structure or internal design of the Software, except to
      the extent that such an act cannot lawfully be prohibited;

   c) modify the Software or create derivative works from it;

   d) remove, obscure or alter any copyright, trademark or other proprietary
      notice contained in or displayed by the Software;

   e) use the Software to provide a service to third parties, or on behalf of
      any organisation other than the Licensee, without prior written consent.

   The Software is licensed, not sold. All intellectual property rights in the
